text:
The Bruins have won four straight and sit at 13-4-1, 27 points, after Sunday's 4-1 win over Florida. Our playoff race gives them an 82% chance of making it and projects about 102 points.

How they're doing it matters. They've outscored teams 67-41, but their share of expected goals (the quality of chances) is close to even at 50.6%. The goaltending has saved 15.4 goals above expected, and the team has finished 9.3 goals above its chances. Jeremy Swayman's 40 saves Sunday were the latest example, and our numbers say Michael DiPietro has been even better than his save rate lately: 4.8 goals saved above expected over his last five starts. By our count Boston has about 7 more points than its play deserves.

The structure is solid. Hampus Lindholm and Charlie McAvoy have taken 63% of the expected goals together and outscored teams 12-3. The Pastrnak-Zacha-Peterka line has been dangerous. The worry is that the other top line just lost James Hagens, on injured reserve for "a few weeks" after a cross-check in Pittsburgh. Nikita Zadorov, fined $5,000 for a punch on Alex Vlasic, keeps showing up in trade talk.

What to watch: whether the second line holds without Hagens, and what happens when the saves come back to normal.
headline: Boston is winning on saves and Pastrnak
